description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:170-238

The doc comment says:

> `pkix-ct`'s `SignedCertificateTimestamp` does not carry an explicit
> `entry_type` field (it is implied by the delivery channel — cert
> extension ⇒ precert_entry, OCSP / TLS-handshake ⇒ x509_entry). This
> function unconditionally treats the SCT as `x509_entry`; the caller
> is responsible for picking the right entry point based on delivery
> channel.

This is a known design choice. The contract problem: when a caller
gets it wrong (passes a `precert_entry` SCT to `verify_sct_for_cert`,
or vice versa), the resulting failure is `Error::InvalidSignature`.

That diagnostic is indistinguishable from:

- Tampered SCT signature
- Wrong cert bytes (caller passed pre-cert when they should have
  passed final cert)
- Wrong log key (caller's log list was stale and the log key
  rotated)
- Right log key, wrong algorithm dispatch

…all of which are real failure modes. A caller debugging an
integration cannot tell from the error which one occurred.

This is a documentation contract failure: the doc warns the caller
to pick correctly, but provides no way to recover from picking
wrong. Three exits:

A. Add an `entry_type` field to `SignedCertificateTimestamp` derived
   from the delivery channel, and have the verifier dispatch
   automatically. The fields the caller would have set are now set
   by `from_extension_value` / `sct_list_from_tls_extension` /
   `sct_list_from_ocsp_response` — those constructors know which
   channel they parsed. This dissolves the issue entirely.

B. Return a typed `Error::EntryTypeMismatch` from the verifier when
   the signature would have verified under the OTHER entry type. The
   verifier would re-attempt with the alternate signed input on
   `InvalidSignature` and surface the alternative if it succeeds.
   Cost: 2x verification work on every error path.

C. Document the failure mode prominently and add a `try_both`
   convenience method on `SctVerifier`. Cheaper than B because the
   caller opts in.

Recommendation: A. The `entry_type` is wire-format information that
SHOULD be on the parsed type; it being implicit is a leak of the
parsing layer into the verification layer. PKIX-ppbr.19 is also a
defensive-code-forcing issue: every caller that handles SCTs from
mixed delivery channels (OCSP + TLS handshake + embedded) has to
maintain its own `(sct, channel)` association and route through the
right verifier.

Priority P1 because this is a contract decision that becomes harder
to make once the API ships and callers have written
delivery-channel-aware code on top.
title: verify_sct_for_cert silently treats every SCT as x509_entry — wrong-entry-type bug surfaces as InvalidSignature
